Page 3
B06-L01 - Integrated DA-to-DE bridge capstone
1. Why it matters
Course 3 should not begin because you finished pages. It should begin because you can connect SQL, Python, modeling,
warehousing, data quality and platform reasoning into one auditable flow and recover when that flow fails.
2. What you are learning
Build and defend the Home Services Network capstone as one evidence chain: source contracts -> SQL -> Python ->
model/history -> warehouse/quality -> platform/monitoring -> reconciliation/recovery -> professional handoff.
3. Prerequisite
Course 1 plus B01-B05 evidence. You are allowed to use the B01-B05 learner books during this guided capstone. The protected
Final Gate comes later and is closed to solution help.
4. Picture it in your head
Picture a relay race. SQL, Python, modeling and cloud reasoning are not separate trophies. Each runner must hand trustworthy
evidence to the next. If one handoff loses rows, changes grain or ignores a failed control, the whole pipeline is untrusted.
5. New words before use
evidence chain
saved proof connecting source assumptions, transformations, controls and final output
trusted publish
output released only after required controls pass
independent reconciliation
a separate check that can detect an error in the main transformation
safe rerun
running unchanged inputs again without duplicating or corrupting trusted business rows
failure recovery
detect -> contain -> diagnose -> repair -> rerun/backfill -> validate -> document
handoff
clear artifacts and explanation another engineer can continue safely
6. Watch / visual source
No new external video is assigned here. This is deliberate: B06-L01 tests transfer of B01-B05, not another tutorial dependency.
Use the course-built architecture/evidence map and your verified B01-B05 sources only when a specific prior skill needs review.
ANALYST -> ENGINEER TRANSITION
What you already know as an analyst: You already know how to produce an analysis using SQL/Python/Power BI and explain a
business result.
What changes in engineering: Engineering requires the entire path to be reproducible, grain-safe, validated, observable enough to
diagnose, and recoverable when something breaks.
Why engineers care: A correct dashboard at the end cannot prove that rows were not silently multiplied, history was not rewritten, a
critical defect was not ignored, or the next rerun will not duplicate trusted data.
Small worked example: Home Services has 72 order rows, 144 item rows and 271 event rows. An engineer keeps those grains
explicit, aggregates items before joining order-level fees, detects the one orphan event, blocks malformed numeric input, proves
historical technician logic, and records safe rerun evidence before calling the output trusted.
Real engineering version: C3 will implement deeper engineering environments, ingestion/state, dbt, orchestration and scale. B06
proves you can enter that course with the prerequisite reasoning already stable.
7. Follow with me once
Open B06_CAPSTONE_EVIDENCE_WORKBOOK_RC1.xlsx -> START_HERE. Then open Source_Contracts. Follow the exact
order shown there. Run B06_PRACTICE_POSTGRESQL_SETUP_RC1.sql when PostgreSQL is available, complete
B06_PRACTICE_SQL_WORKSPACE_RC1.sql, then complete B06_PRACTICE_PIPELINE_NOTEBOOK_RC1.ipynb. Save every
validation and failure result; do not overwrite failed attempts.
8. What you should see
Your evidence should reconcile the published order-level result to lower-grain items, show source lineage, expose rather than hide
quality failures, distinguish current vs historical technician attributes, define platform/access/refresh/monitoring choices, and prove
an unchanged rerun is safe.
9. Why it worked
The capstone starts from contracts and controls, not from a dashboard. That makes every later step testable: source grain ->
transformation grain -> key/cardinality proof -> quality action -> publish decision -> rerun/recovery evidence.
10. Common beginner mistakes
Joining item/event/skill rows directly to order-level fees; using DISTINCT to hide fan-out; coercing BAD_AMOUNT to zero and
publishing anyway; using current technician region for historical facts without a decision; treating a successful run as proof; writing
a cloud diagram with no access/freshness/failure owner.
11. If stuck
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B06 Capstone & C3 Entry | INTERNAL QA RC1
Page 4
Use the evidence workbook one sheet at a time. Ask: What is one row? What must be unique? What can multiply? What
independent check could catch me? What blocks publish? What is saved if this fails? Who owns the next action?
12. Small version alone
After the guided Home Services attempt is complete, change the serving grain to technician-month and rebuild only the necessary
SQL/model/reconciliation evidence without copying your first wording. Preserve one trusted order-value control.
13. Validate
Capstone is not complete until the workbook has evidence across all eight readiness areas, required controls reconcile, one critical
failure is demonstrated and contained, an unchanged rerun is proven safe, and the handoff states one limitation plus owner/next
action.
14. Teach it back
Explain the complete capstone in 90 seconds without naming tools first. Start with source grains and business contracts, then
describe transformations, quality gates, history, recovery and handoff.
15. Protected review + changed retry
Save the complete first capstone attempt before opening B06_CAPSTONE_PRACTICE_REVIEW_PROTECTED_RC1.pdf.
Compare only the weak area, close the review, and perform the assigned changed transfer. Append repair evidence; never erase
the first attempt.
16. Evidence / mastery + next route
Required: completed evidence workbook, SQL file, notebook, validation/run evidence, failure/recovery proof, changed transfer and
handoff defense. PASS -> B06-L02. Weak area -> targeted B01-B05 or B06 repair only; do not restart Course 2B.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B06 Capstone & C3 Entry | INTERNAL QA RC1
Page 5
B06-L02 - Course 3 entry readiness and handoff
1. Why it matters
A completion percentage can hide a critical gap. Course 3 assumes you can reason independently about data correctness and
handoff, but it does not assume you already know Linux, Git workflows, virtual environments, Docker or other C3-00
implementation topics.
2. What you are learning
Take the protected Final Gate, score evidence against the eight readiness floors, route any weakness to the exact repair, and
produce an explicit C3 handoff with no hidden prerequisites.
3. Prerequisite
B06-L01 capstone evidence complete. Gate A is the first protected assessment. Review/solution material stays closed until the
attempt is saved.
4. Picture it in your head
Picture an airport gate with eight document checks. You do not board because 95% of the checklist is green if the passport check
fails. But you also are not required to already know how to fly the airplane. B06 checks entry readiness; C3 teaches the next
engineering environment and systems depth.
5. New words before use
readiness floor
minimum evidence level required in one competency; not an average
critical failure
a defect that blocks a pass regardless of average performance
protected attempt
independent assessment completed before opening its review
full reassessment
fresh Gate B/C only when explicitly assigned after broad/critical instability
entry ready
Final Gate PASS + every floor met + no unresolved critical blocker
hidden prerequisite
skill demanded for entry even though it was never explicitly taught beforehand
6. Watch / visual source
No external video is assigned. Open B06_C3_ENTRY_READINESS_SCORECARD_RC1.xlsx -> C3_00_Preview. It lists the 12
incoming C3-00 topics and explicitly marks each as taught in C3, not a Bridge pass requirement.
ANALYST -> ENGINEER TRANSITION
What you already know as an analyst: You already know how to judge whether an analysis is correct enough to present and how to
revise weak work.
What changes in engineering: Engineering progression uses competency floors, protected independent evidence, critical-failure
blockers and explicit remediation routes rather than course-completion percentages.
Why engineers care: Without floors, one strong area can mathematically hide a dangerous weakness. Without an explicit C3
boundary, learners waste time pre-learning Linux/Git/Docker or arrive believing unexplained prerequisites were missed.
Small worked example: Scores SQL=3, Python=3, Modeling=3, Warehousing=3, Quality=3, Independent=3, Cloud=2, Ownership=2
plus Final Gate PASS -> C3 ENTRY READY. If Python=2, overall status stays NOT READY even if every other score is 4.
Real engineering version: After entry, C3-00 teaches role shift, Linux/WSL2, shell, Git, venv/dependency pinning,
modules/packages/project structure, config/secrets, logging, tests, CLI, Docker and idempotence/runbooks from zero.
7. Follow with me once
Open B06_FINAL_GATE_RULES_RC1.pdf before starting only to understand allowed materials and evidence. Then take Gate A
from Assessment/Gate_A. Save the complete attempt. Only after that open B06_GATE_A_REVIEW_PROTECTED_RC1.pdf. If
PASS, complete the readiness scorecard. If repair is required, follow the named route. Gate B/C remain sealed unless explicitly
assigned.
8. What you should see
The scorecard stays NOT READY until every readiness floor and the Final Gate condition are satisfied. The C3_00_Preview sheet
marks all 12 incoming engineering-foundation topics as "No - taught in C3" under pre-entry requirement.
9. Why it worked
Separate floors prevent averaging away critical weaknesses. Protected reassessment prevents learning the exact answer instead
of proving the skill. The preview matrix prevents the Bridge from expanding into Course 3.
10. Common beginner mistakes
Marking READY from percentage completion; opening Gate B for extra practice; averaging a 2 in Python against a 4 in SQL;
treating C3-00 Linux/Git/Docker as missing Bridge content; erasing failed attempts after a later pass.
11. If stuck
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B06 Capstone & C3 Entry | INTERNAL QA RC1
Page 6
Use the scorecard row that failed. Follow its Repair_Routing entry. Repair only that competency on changed evidence, then take
the reassessment route actually assigned by the protected review.
12. Small version alone
Given a mock readiness profile with one weak area, decide READY/NOT READY, name the exact repair module, and explain why
no other module should be restarted.
13. Validate
Entry status is READY only when SQL/Python/modeling/warehousing/data quality/independent analysis >=3; Cloud/Fabric and
professional ownership >=2; Final Gate PASS; no unresolved critical blocker; and integrated capstone evidence exists.
14. Teach it back
Explain the difference between "Bridge complete", "C3 entry ready", and "job-ready Data Engineer" in plain language. Then name
three C3-00 topics you are explicitly allowed to learn after entry.
15. Protected review + changed retry
Save the Gate attempt first. Review only the attempted variant. Perform targeted repair on changed evidence. Gate B/C are full
reassessments, not practice sheets, and open only when assigned. Attempt history remains append-only.
16. Evidence / mastery + next route
Required: protected Gate pass, completed readiness scorecard, repair history if any, and C3 handoff. PASS -> begin C3-00. NOT
READY -> exact targeted repair. This course never declares you already job-ready as a Data Engineer.

masteryCheck.text:
C2B / B06 / ASTRA PARITY RC4
B06 Bridge Mastery Check
Closed-book cross-module synthesis - non-gating
C2B / B06 / CHECKPOINT46
Page 1
Non-gating Bridge Mastery Check
This does not replace the guided capstone, Final Gate or readiness scorecard. Save a genuine
closed-book attempt before the protected review.
Fresh synthesis prompt
- Given three monthly service-order files, an item table, event JSON, technician current/history tables, skill
memberships, regional targets and mixed platform sources, state every source grain/key before writing
SQL or Python.
- Design a deterministic Python ingestion/validation flow that blocks malformed numeric input and
duplicate technician keys before trusted publish; include source lineage and safe rerun evidence.
- Write the SQL/model contract that prevents base fee, item value and events from multiplying each other.
Include one window/time comparison and one independent control query.
- Design technician history with business key, surrogate/version key and fact lookup rule; explain one Type
1 vs Type 2 attribute choice.
- Define at least eight quality checks with BLOCK/WARN actions, owners and publish consequences.
- Design private-vs-cloud connection/access/freshness/monitoring treatment without requiring a live
tenant.
- Write the handoff: scope, architecture, controls, failure recovery, known limitation, owner and next action.

C2B / B06 / ASTRA PARITY RC4 / CHECKPOINT46
Page 2
Evidence to save
- Grain/key/source inventory.
- SQL controls + fan-out proof.
- Python run/validation/recovery evidence.
- Model/history contract.
- Quality contract and reconciliations.
- Platform/freshness/monitoring decisions.
- Professional handoff and 60-90 second defense.
Pass standard
Mastery requires a reproducible evidence chain. The check stays non-gating and cannot mark C3 ENTRY
READY.

C2B / B06 / ASTRA PARITY RC4
B06 Bridge Mastery Protected Review
Review, close, changed retry, preserve evidence history
C2B / B06 / CHECKPOINT46
Page 1
Protected review - saved genuine attempt required
Diagnose the saved attempt, close this review, then complete the changed retry without copying its
wording.
Strong synthesis pattern
- State grains and keys before joins. Aggregate child facts before combining transaction measures.
- Python validates schema/types/keys before merge; critical defects block trusted publish; source lineage
and run evidence are saved.
- Current vs historical attributes are deliberate and facts resolve to the correct historical version.
- Targets and other higher-grain facts are compared only at compatible grain.
- Platform design starts from location/sensitivity/freshness/identity and has monitoring/recovery ownership.
- Reconciliation is independent evidence, not the same transformation repeated twice.

C2B / B06 / ASTRA PARITY RC4 / CHECKPOINT46
Page 2
Changed retry
- Move the private orders source to a cloud SaaS API and tighten event freshness to five minutes. Change
only the affected connectivity/refresh/monitoring design.
- Add a fourth monthly file and a duplicate master key. Prove the pipeline detects the key defect and
remains rerunnable after repair.
- Change technician region from Type 2 to Type 1 while specialty remains Type 2. Explain fact lookup
impact.
- Save the retry separately; this review never authorizes Gate B/C or C3 entry.

C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B06 Capstone & C3 Entry | INTERNAL QA RC1
Page 1
B06 Capstone Practice Review - Protected
OPEN ONLY AFTER the complete Home Services capstone attempt is saved. Close this review before changed transfer.
The capstone has many valid implementations. Compare your evidence against the controls below rather than copying one exact
solution.
Review 1 - SQL and reconciliation
Strong: explicit source/result grains, order-level economics built safely from item grain, staged CTE/window/time logic, quality
defects exposed, and an independent reconciliation. Critical weak patterns: fee/count multiplied by child rows; DISTINCT used as
a bandage; nondeterministic window order; "validation" repeats the same query. Changed transfer: rebuild technician-month
output while preserving one independent order-value control.
Review 2 - Python automation
Strong: deterministic file discovery, source lineage, schema/type/key validation before merge, critical defect blocking/quarantine,
publish only after controls, saved validation/log/manifest and safe unchanged rerun. Critical weak patterns: hard-coded hidden
state, BAD_AMOUNT silently coerced, duplicate technician key allowed, BLOCK failure logged but trusted publish continues.
Changed transfer: move input folder and add a fourth monthly file; change configuration/path, not core logic.

C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B06 Capstone & C3 Entry | INTERNAL QA RC1
Page 2
Review 3 - Modeling, history and warehouse
Strong: order/item/event/target/membership grains stay explicit; fact/dimension/bridge and cardinality are justified; current vs
historical technician attributes are deliberate; SCD business/surrogate key reasoning is documented; layers have source-of-truth
and replay contracts. Changed transfer: specialty Type 1, region Type 2; explain different attribute treatment and historical fact
lookup.
Review 4 - Platform, monitoring and ownership
Strong: source location/sensitivity/SLA drive connection, identity, access and refresh decisions; private source path differs from
cloud/SaaS; monitoring separates auth/network/schema/data failures; recovery has owner + post-recovery validation. Changed
transfer: move Orders_DB from private/on-prem to cloud SaaS and tighten event SLA to five minutes; update only affected design.

C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B06 Capstone & C3 Entry | INTERNAL QA RC1
Page 3
Review 5 - C3 entry readiness
Do not average away a weak critical area. Required floors: SQL/Python/modeling/warehousing/data quality/independent analysis
>=3; Cloud/Fabric and professional ownership >=2; Final Gate PASS. Repair only the exact failed competency. This review does
not authorize Gate B/C; full reassessment must be explicitly assigned.
